dedupe_keys.name: paz x band sar data through esa third party missions

description: PAZ is a Spanish high-resolution X-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite launched on 22 February 2018, owned and operated by Hisdesat, that flies in the same orbit as TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X and works with them as a constellation. It is in a polar dawn-dusk sun-synchronous orbit at 514 km with an 11-day repeat cycle and a mean revisit of 24 hours, using ground stations in Madrid and the Canary Islands, and its radar operates in modes from staring spotlight (0.25 m) through spotlight and stripmap (3 m) to wide ScanSAR (270 by 200 km). Through ESA's Third Party Missions programme, which covers more than 50 missions, the PAZ ESA archive collection is freely available to researchers worldwide, sample data can be downloaded, and incident angle information has been added to the PAZ and TerraSAR-X and TanDEM-X collections. Access for research is free under ESA's Third Party Missions terms, through a project proposal or the open archive; no separate licence is named on the page read. Caveats: the mission serves both civilian and security and defence needs, and the free archive is aimed at researchers. Coverage is global. It supports hazard exposure and emergency response analysis, such as flood mapping and ground deformation near infrastructure with high-resolution radar; related records are the RADARSAT Constellation Mission data and the CONAE geoportal.
